disease: Fragile X syndrome (FMR1 CGG-repeat full-mutation promoter hypermethylation silencing; FRAXA)
suspended_reason: The cause is a REPEAT-EXPANSION-DRIVEN PROMOTER METHYLATION SILENCING, not a sequence-level promoter switch the kit can read. In the unaffected population the FMR1 5'-UTR carries ~5-44 CGG repeats; a premutation (~55-200) expands, on MATERNAL transmission, to a FULL MUTATION (>200, often 500-1000+ CGG) -- and the full-mutation expansion triggers CpG-island HYPERMETHYLATION of the FMR1 promoter, packaging it into heterochromatin and TRANSCRIPTIONALLY SILENCING FMR1, so FMRP (the synaptic translational repressor) is lost -> intellectual disability, autism, macro-orchidism, the fragile X phenotype. The defining feature for this kit is that the repeats do NOT alter the FMRP CODING sequence and do NOT change the promoter SEQUENCE the engine reads: the lesion is the (a) repeat COPY NUMBER and (b) the resulting CpG METHYLATION STATE -- both INVISIBLE to a nearest-neighbour stacking gamma read of the reference promoter. The FMR1 promoter is in fact perfectly readable as DNA (cached gamma 1.4563, chrX; it carries the HIGHEST CpG density in the kit's whole panel at 0.0508 -- i.e. it IS a strong CpG island, exactly the substrate that gets methylation-silenced in the full mutation), but the engine reads the UNMETHYLATED REFERENCE state and has no channel for methylation or repeat-length, so it cannot read the silencing lesion. This opens a SEVENTH held MECHANISM CLASS -- repeat-EXPANSION-driven promoter CpG-METHYLATION SILENCING -- genuinely distinct from the six already held: (1) whole-chromosome ANEUPLOIDY (Down); (2) IMPRINTING (Prader-Willi / Angelman / Beckwith-Wiedemann); (3) repeat-CONTRACTION-driven chromatin DEREPRESSION (FSHD / DUX4); (4)-(5) the MITOCHONDRIAL GENOME (LHON / MELAS point mutations; Kearns-Sayre structural deletion); (6) the contiguous-gene MICRODELETION (22q11.2). It is the precise MIRROR of the FSHD hold: FSHD is a repeat CONTRACTION that DE-REPRESSES (activates) a silenced gene (DUX4), whereas fragile X is a repeat EXPANSION that SILENCES (represses) an active gene (FMR1) -- the same repeat/epigenetic axis, opposite direction. It is also the sharp same-gene-FAMILY contrast to Huntington (already RESOLVED): both are trinucleotide-repeat-expansion diseases, but HTT's CAG expansion is in the CODING region and produces a TOXIC protein the engine reads at the locus-switch level (resolved), whereas FMR1's CGG expansion is in the 5'-UTR / PROMOTER and acts by METHYLATION SILENCING the engine cannot read (suspended) -- coding-toxic-gain vs promoter-epigenetic-silencing on the same class of lesion. Like the mtDNA and microdeletion holds, fragile X is suspended PURELY on engine-readability, NOT for lack of therapy: there is no approved disease-modifying therapy (FMR1-reactivation / promoter-demethylation strategies -- e.g. CRISPR-dCas9 demethylation, 5-azacytidine -- have not restored meaningful FMRP, and the mGluR5 / GABA-B trials [mavoglurant, arbaclofen] addressed downstream signalling, not the silencing), so the hold keys on whether the engine can READ the lesion, not on whether one can treat it. Prevalence ~1:4,000 males, ~1:8,000 females -- the commonest inherited cause of intellectual disability. Disclosed, not dropped. (Verkerk 1991 Cell 65:905 [FMR1 cloning / CGG repeat]; Pieretti 1991 Cell 66:817 [methylation silencing]; Oberle 1991 Science 252:1097 [unstable DNA / methylation]).
discipline: no analyzable single-gene DNA read -> held (author's rule). Disclosed, not dropped.
